{{nowrap|[[Detroit Country Day School|Detroit Country Day]] (Detroit, Michigan)}} | college = [[Detroit Titans men's basketball|Detroit]] (2010–2013) | draft_year = 2013 | draft_round = TBD | draft_pick = TBD | draft_team = | career_start = | career_end = | years1 = | team1 = | years2 = | team2 = | highlights = * [[Horizon League Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Horizon League Player of the Year]] (2013) * 2× First Team All-Conference (2012, 2013) * [[Horizon League]] Newcomer of the Year (2011) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's High School All-American]] ([[2010 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2010]]) }} '''Ray McCallum, Jr.''' (born June 12, 1991) is an American basketball player. In the [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]], he was named the [[Horizon League Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Horizon League Player of the Year]] after leading the [[Horizon League]] in scoring at 18.7 points per game and guiding the [[Detroit Titans men's basketball|Detroit Titans]] to a berth in the [[2013 National Invitation Tournament]].{{cite web| title =Detroit's Ray McCallum Jr. named Horizon League player of the year| publisher =''[[The Detroit News]]''| date =March 4, 2013| url =http://www.detroitnews.com/article/20130304/SPORTS0203/303040405| accessdate =April 3, 2013}}{{cite web| title =Ray McCallum stats| work =sports-reference.com| publisher =Sports Reference LLC| date =March 30, 2013| url =http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/ray-mccallum-2.html|accessdate = April 3, 2013}} McCallum also averaged 4.5 assists, 5.1 rebounds and 1.9 steals per game. He is considered a likely [[2013 NBA Draft]] prospect{{cite web| last =Markowski| first =Tom| title =Scout: Detroit's Ray McCallum Jr. a certain first-rounder in NBA draft| publisher =''The Detroit News''| date =February 27, 2013| url =http://www.detroitnews.com/article/20130227/SPORTS0203/302270353| accessdate = April 3, 2013}}{{cite web| title =Ray McCallum, Jr.| work =NBADraft.net| publisher =Sports Phenoms, Inc.| year=2013| url =http://nbadraft.net/players/ray-mccallum| accessdate = April 3, 2013}} after choosing to forgo his [[senior (education)|senior]] year and enter the draft as an underclassman.{{cite web|title =Ray McCallum entering NBA draft| publisher =ESPN| date =April 28, 2013| url =http://espn.go.com/nba/draft2013/story/_/id/9221920/ray-mccallum-decides-leave-detroit-titans-nba-draft| accessdate = April 30, 2013}} ==High school== The first two years of McCallum's high school career were spent at [[Bloomington High School North]] in [[Bloomington, Indiana]].{{cite web| title =Ray McCallum, Jr. bio| work =Detroit Titans| publisher =University of Detroit Mercy| year=2013| url =http://www.detroittitans.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=1402| accessdate =April 3, 2013}} He then attended [[Detroit Country Day School]] in [[Detroit, Michigan]] for his final two years. In McCallum's senior season in 2009–10, he led Detroit Country Day to a state championship; in the final against [[J. W. Sexton High School|J. W. Sexton]], they won 71–47 behind McCallum's 32 points, eight rebounds and seven steals. For the season he averaged 22.5 points, 7.5 rebounds and 5.5 assists per game. McCallum placed third in voting for the Michigan's Mr. Basketball award, was named to the All-State Dream Teams produced by the ''[[Detroit Free Press]]'' and ''[[The Detroit News]]'', and was a consensus Top 50 player coming out of high school. ''[[Parade (magazine)|Parade]]'' magazine named him an All-American, as did [[McDonald]]'s. McCallum played in the [[2010 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2010 McDonald's All-American Game]] and recorded four points, two rebounds and one steal. ==College== Ray McCallum, Jr. chose to play at the [[University of Detroit Mercy]] for his father, Titans head coach [[Ray McCallum]]. He was "one of the most highly-recruited players in school history" and passed on scholarship offers from schools such as [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[Oklahoma Sooners men's basketball|Oklahoma]] and [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]]. In his rookie season in [[2010–11 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2009–10]], he became the first player from the University of Detroit to make an all-Horizon League Team as a [[freshman]], where he earned second team honors. McCallum led his team in scoring (13.5) assists (4.9 apg) and total steals (54). [[CollegeInsider.com]] named him to their Freshman All-America squad, and his 157 assists during the regular season was second in the [[NCAA]] among freshmen. On February 16, he almost recorded a [[triple-double]] against [[Youngstown State Penguins men's basketball|Youngstown State]] with 14 points, 10 rebounds and 8 assists. McCallum followed up his strong freshman campaign with a strong [[sophomore]] year effort. He averaged 15.4 points, 4.5 rebounds, 4.0 assists and 1.6 steals per game en route to first team all-conference honors. Detroit finished with a 22–14 overall record, making it to the first round of the [[2012 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]]. McCallum was named a [[Bob Cousy Award]] Final 20 honoree. In [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13]], his [[junior (education)|junior]] year, McCallum became the first player since [[2000–01 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2000–01]] to be named the preseason [[Horizon League Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Horizon League Player of the Year]] and to earn that honor during the postseason as well (Detroit's [[Rashad Phillips]] had previously been named both). Even though he led the conference in scoring at 18.7 points per game, Detroit finished in second place in the regular season, did not win the conference tournament championship, and were thus relegated to a [[National Invitation Tournament]] (NIT) berth. They finished the year with a 20–13 overall record. ==Professional== On April 27, 2013, McCallum announced that he was leaving school after his junior season and that he was officially declaring himself eligible for the [[2013 NBA Draft]]. ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== *[http://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/ray-mccallum-2.html Ray McCallum, Jr.] @ sports-reference.com *[http://www.detroittitans.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=1402 Ray McCallum, Jr.]'s Detroit profile {{Horizon League Men's Basketball Player of the Year navbox}} {{Persondata | NAME = McCallum, Ray, Jr. | ALTERNATIVE NAMES = | SHORT DESCRIPTION = American basketball player | DATE OF BIRTH = June 12, 1991 | PLACE OF BIRTH = Detroit, Michigan | DATE OF DEATH = | PLACE OF DEATH = }} {{DEFAULTSORT:McCallum, Ray, Jr.}} [[Category:1991 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:Basketball players from Michigan]] [[Category:Detroit Titans men's basketball players]] [[Category:McDonald's High School All-Americans]] [[Category:Parade High School All-Americans (boys' basketball)]] [[Category:Point guards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Detroit, Michigan]]
